signals.text: Whole School learning Experiences: Bosham Curriculum
At Bosham Primary School, we also model the application of the alphabetic code through phonics in shared reading and writing, both inside and outside the phonics lesson and across the curriculum.

We start teaching phonics in Reception and follow the Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised progression, system which ensures children build on their growing knowledge of the alphabetic code, mastering phonics to read and spell as they move through school.

Welcome
Welcome to our school. We are very proud to be able to share with you the wonderful opportunities that we provide for the children here at Bosham Primary School.
Do you have a child starting school in September 2026?
If you would like to visit our school please call the school office
on 01243 572375 to arrange a tour.
To apply for a school place please click the West Sussex Admissions link below:
West Sussex Admissions link
Bosham Primary School is a vibrant and thriving village school where children are enthusiastic and motivated to achieve across all areas of their learning. Children are at the very heart of every decision we make. Everything we do is designed to create the very best learning environment we can to enable all of our children to thrive. We want all of our pupils to leave us as children who are:
Resilient
Independent
Creative
Emotionally intelligent
Through our rich, engaging and challenging curriculum, we ensure that all children are encouraged to develop a passion for life-long learning and curiosity that helps develop high aspirations and a lifetime of memories.
We have a dedicated team that is constantly striving to promote high standards in everything we do and this is further embedded through our successful relationships with parents, the local community and the other schools in the local area. We firmly believe that education is a partnership between home and school and regard you as an active partner in your child's education and value your support.
I hope that this website will give you as much information as possible about our school, the staff and the many activities that our children enjoy through our curriculum and our extracurricular activities.
If you are considering Bosham Primary as the school for your child, please do come and visit us; we would be delighted to show you around and answer any questions you may have. To arrange this, either email Mrs Walster at office@boshamprimary.co.uk or call the school on 01243 572375.

pageCache.text:
Breakfast & After School Provision
Breakfast Club
At Bosham, we are delighted to be able to offer a thriving breakfast club which offers a safe, happy and caring environment for your children, from 7:45am until school starts.
These clubs are run by qualified, experienced members of school staff who are known by the children and a range of child-led activities are organised each day.
Breakfast Club cost = £5.00 a session and free for pupil premium children
We provide breakfast in the morning from a selection of:
Please do speak to a member of staff should you wish your child to have something specific, so we can cater for a variety of diets. If you have any queries, please speak to Mrs Walster in the school office 01243 572375.
crumpets
various spreads
milk and water to drink
After school club
Active8 Minds run the after-school club at Bosham Primary School. The club runs until 18:00 Monday to Friday. Please see their website for further information and how to book a place for your child.
https://active8minds.co.uk/
The Family Information Service provides information about services offered to families within West Sussex, including how they can help families find childcare.
For full information about the activities and family support they can offer, please click on the link below to their website.
www.westsussex.gov.uk/fis

​​Reading & Phonics
Phonics
At Bosham Primary School, we believe that all our children can become fluent readers and writers. This is why we teach reading through Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised, which is a systematic and synthetic early reading and phonics programme. We start teaching phonics in Reception and follow the Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised progression, system which ensures children build on their growing knowledge of the alphabetic code, mastering phonics to read and spell as they move through school.
As a result, all our children are able to tackle any unfamiliar words as they read. At Bosham Primary School, we also model the application of the alphabetic code through phonics in shared reading and writing, both inside and outside the phonics lesson and across the curriculum. We have a strong focus on language development for our children because we know that speaking and listening are crucial skills for reading and writing in all subjects.
Comprehension
At Bosham Primary School, we value reading as a crucial life skill. By the time children leave us, they read confidently for meaning and regularly enjoy reading for pleasure. Our readers are equipped with the tools to tackle unfamiliar vocabulary. We encourage our children to see themselves as readers for both pleasure and purpose.
Because we believe teaching every child to read is so important, our English leader drives the early reading programme in our school. They monitor and support our reading team, so everyone teaches with fidelity to the Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised programme.
Please click on the links below to find out more about how we teach phonics and how you can support your child at home with their reading development.
https://www.littlewandlelettersandsounds.org.uk/resources/for-parents/
The resources on this page will help you support your child by saying their sounds and writing their letters. There are also some useful videos: you can see how children are taught at school and feel confident about supporting their reading at home.
Reading KS2
The school uses the Jane Considine 'Hooked on Books' approach to reading and spelling. Reading is crucial to children's development and potential for success in life. Research shows that children who read books often at age 10 and continue to read through adolescence, gain higher results in maths, vocabulary and spelling tests at age 16 than those who read less regularly.
Nothing is more important in education than ensuring that every child can read well. Pupils who can read are overwhelmingly more likely to succeed at school, achieve good qualifications, and subsequently enjoy a fulfilling and rewarding career.

Governors
​Bosham Primary School Governor Vision
“Nurturing the potential of all children by providing strategic direction, support and robust governance in partnership with our senior leadership team.”
Most questions that you have about the school can be answered by your child’s teacher or by contacting the Headteacher, or any member of the Leadership Team. The governors, however, are always happy to hear from you if you have a question or comment about the school.
You can contact the chair, Lou Adams, via email: ladams@boshamprimary.co.uk or write to Lou c/o Bosham Primary School.
Lou Adams - Chair of Governors
I live in Bosham and have 3 daughters; one who is currently a pupil at Bosham and two who have left to go to senior school. I feel incredibly privileged to be a Governor of Bosham Primary School, which has had such an impact on my own children and so many others.
Professionally, I have over 25 years' experience in leadership across healthcare, the private sector and the charity sector. I began my career as a children's nurse before moving into senior leadership within the NHS. Today, I work as Chief of Staff in an international technology company, bringing experience in strategy, governance and organisational leadership.
I believe every child deserves an excellent education in a safe, ambitious and nurturing environment. As a governing board, our role is to provide strategic leadership, robust challenge and unwavering support to ensure Bosham Primary School continues to flourish for every child and every family in our community.
Charlotte Weller - Vice Chair/FP
Hello, my name is Charlotte Weller, and I have been the Vice Chair in role since May 2025. I live in Bosham with my husband, Giles, and our two boys, Ralph and Arlo. It has been wonderful watching their knowledge and confidence grow at BPS, so I applied for the role because I was keen to support and contribute to the ongoing development of the school.
In my day job I am an Operations Manager at WSCC, so I have lots of experience working with communities trying to achieve positive outcomes with limited funding. Outside of work, I love spending time with my family and friends....mainly outside, trying to get rid of the boys' energy!
Megan Clay - SEN/Policies
Hi there - I'm a Parent Governor and joined the Board in December 2022. With a daughter at BPS, I am looking forward to working with the other governors to support our super village school and ensure it thrives. I am a solicitor by profession and work for an environmental law charity during the week. At the weekends, you can find me on bike rides with the kids, running the coast path or getting out (or in) the water!
Chris Dring - Curriculum EYFS
I was previously Chair of Governors at Bosham Primary School and also a governor at Chi High. I have been a governor at Bosham Primary School since 2020 and have a grandchild at the school. I am a parent to 2 daughters and have 4 delightful grandchildren. I have lived in Chichester for 20 years and used to work at Chichester District Council. I enjoy walking, playing netball, and I am a passionate West Ham fan; you might notice my scarf!
I regularly pick up my grandchild on a Friday, so please stop me and ask about the work of the governing body and our current focus.
Marcus Munt
I first moved to Bosham in 2004 and discovered what a wonderful village this is. I live on Bosham Lane with my wife and son. I enjoy spending time on the water and have a boat that is moored in the village. I love to travel, and I have a particular soft spot for Africa. I have also taken part in several charity car rallies to Europe and North Africa.
I have always worked in the commercial sector, primarily in sales and marketing roles and, beyond this, have sat on industry committees, latterly as chairman. Like many people during the recent pandemic, I tried to give a little back and I did this by volunteering at the Chichester Vaccination Centre and St Wilfrid’s Hospice.
As a governor of BPS, I wanted to put my professional skills to use in a way that helps the community that I live in. Hopefully, the school and the current governors will find me a useful addition to the team and I hope that I will also learn a great deal along the way.
Dinah O'Hana-James - Pupil Premium
Hi – I’m Dinah. I was elected to the governing body in October 2025 as a parent governor (mum to Bo and Kit). As a parent governor, my role is to represent the views of the parent body, so please do come and say hello if you’d like to share any thoughts or ideas.
In my professional life, I’ve worked in education for 20 years: in the classroom, as a school leader and as a local authority adviser. This experience has allowed me to see what best practice looks like across many schools, and I aim to bring that knowledge – being committed, curious, challenging, collaborative and creative – to support the strategic direction of our school.
Jenny Upjohn - LA governor / Curriculum Chair KS2
Hello. I am Jenny Upjohn and I am the Local Authority governor, elected in March 2025. I have lived in Bosham all my life and have had links with the school in many capacities over the years, including past pupil and as a parent.
Professionally, I have been in the primary education sector for over 30 years and still teach part-time in another local school. As governor of Bosham Primary School, I will support the school’s clarity of vision, ethos and strategic direction to ensure the best possible outcomes for pupils at the school.
Sue Lambert - Curriculum KS1
Hello - I am Sue. I have lived in Bosham for 26 years, raising a family in the village. My husband and I still live locally and continue to be involved in village life.
We have always been grateful for the education and life experiences that our children received at Bosham Primary School, and it has been a privilege to serve on the governing body since November 2024.
My professional background is in education, having taught in primary schools in London, Hampshire and West Sussex. I also worked as a teaching assistant and in a local nursery school before retiring. My special responsibility as a governor is with Key Stage 1.
Anelise Sinclair-Small - Safeguarding
Hello, my name is Anelise. I live locally with my family. I have a huge passion for travel and I love to be creative. I am a previous BPS parent and was elected to the board in October 2025, as I was keen to join the board to support the ongoing growth and development of the school.
My role within the governing board is to help close the link between the designated safeguarding leads and the board, thus ensuring safe and effective safeguarding of our pupils.
By profession, I am a midwife, currently specialising in child protection and safeguarding children. A family-focused approach is always at the forefront of my mind when supporting children and their families.
I feel extremely privileged to be a governor within the village and look forward to expanding my knowledge and learning of the complexities of safeguarding within the school setting.

To download a copy of this image please click on the link at the bottom of the page called 'Bosham Primary School Learning Experiences'.
Whole School learning Experiences
Once a year, the whole school plans a shared learning experience where we focus on one thing. This year we focused upon developing the pupil's understanding of different parts of the world. Every class choose one country from the seven continents where they studied about their key physical and human characteristics. They learnt about their culture and shared this knowledge with other clases becoming the 'teachers' for the day. At the end of the learning experience all of the children voted for which class was the most persuasive and where they would like to visit the most. This year our Oppys (YR) class were the most persuasive as our children wanted to visit Antartica after their presentation in assembly.
The children also looked at famous artists from the countries and cretaed this fabulous pieces. These pieces of artwork had all of the class contributing of them and we are really proud of them. You can see them hanging up around our school.
In February 2023, this was Change Sings by Amanda Gorman, who is an American poet and activist. Every child in our school undertook an activity to make positive change in our local area. This included litter picking, painting the school fence and many other useful activities that helped other people in our community.
Our authentic outcome for this was to create inspirational art based on the work of different graffiti artists, such as Thierry Noir, Keith Haring, My Dog Sighs and Deborah Shapiro. Here are some of the examples you can see now hung up around the school.
